questions.question: When coupling a trailer, you should:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Connect any glad hands together.
Leave one pair of glad hands loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When connecting air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Release the brakes.
Speed up.
Turn the steering wheel quickly left, then right.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. The trailer will straighten out once traction returns.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a serious leak. The valve closes automatically if air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When braking with an anti-lock brake system, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Use extra hard braking force.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: With an anti-lock brake system, brake the same way you would with a regular brake system.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.
Directly next to the trailer.
Parallel to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Back up straight in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Make quick, sudden changes.
Avoid sudden movements.
Press the accelerator all the way down.

questions.explanation: To prevent tipping when driving with a trailer, steer gently and smoothly. Avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have anti-lock braking systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have anti-lock braking systems (ABS).

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, you should:

options.text: Not use the trailer hand brake.
Brake hard.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake because braking caused the problem.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than normal.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: With an anti-lock brake system, apply your brakes the same way you would with a regular brake system.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic while driving a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for you.
Wait for a large gap in traffic before crossing.
Rely only on your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap in traffic before crossing.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Wait for a large enough gap in traffic to safely cross.

questions.question: When glad hands are coupled, the seals should be pressed together at a ____ angle.

options.text: 50-degree
180-degree
90-degree

questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, you should:

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Activate the emergency brake.
Disconnect the glad hands.

questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
You will stop the vehicle too quickly.
It can cause a skid.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in its ____ position.

options.text: Emergency
Supply
Normal

questions.explanation: The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Motion for another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency authorities.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking by reducing brake pressure when needed.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, maintain a following distance of at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle.

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded: blue for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Place cargo as low as possible in a trailer. A top-heavy vehicle is more likely to roll over.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Lighter than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are harder to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.
